key_facts: The Trump administration decided not to renew the U.S.-Mexico-Canada Agreement on July 1 during a mandatory six-year review, triggering annual reviews instead.

Article 34.7 of USMCA makes six-year check-ins a standing requirement, and having declined to confirm this year, Washington triggered compressed annual reviews until renewal or the agreement lapses in 2036.
Chinese investments in Mexico's automotive sector have reportedly been stalled or canceled pending the review.
Canada adopted 100 percent tariffs on Chinese electric vehicles in 2024 following bilateral coordination with the United States.
Mexico raised tariffs on a range of Chinese imports in 2025, reportedly influenced by sustained U.S. pressure.
